canonical_data: Per-task execution traces, screenshots, replay recordings and compressed step-history chunks written locally, plus a Markdown task plan in the planning profile
current_repo_note: Covers the Android automation agent and its MCP server in this repository, which the README positions for mobile testing as well as everyday tasks. The third_party folder holds portions of Minitap's mobile-use project under its own Apache-2.0 licence file. The advertised AndroidWorld result is the maintainers' own measurement and is not reviewed here.
strengths: Two execution profiles with different failure behaviour: a fast reactive loop that compresses history instead of capping turns, and a planner, operator, and verifier graph that checks a target against the live screen before acting and returns blocked actions for recovery
Telemetry, replay recording, and structured final reports make a run inspectable after the fact, and the on-device helper can be removed or declined
Reachable from coding assistants through an MCP server and from test suites through a typed Python SDK, so one agent serves interactive and CI use
weaknesses: The repository was created in August 2026 and its headline 99 percent AndroidWorld figure is a self-reported result with no independent reproduction
It installs an accessibility service on the target phone, a broad permission that the README discloses and lets the operator opt out of
Its reach is limited to Android devices, since iOS support is a roadmap item, and the traces and plans it keeps are run outputs rather than content a person edits to steer later runs
why_it_matters: A Google-hosted mobile computer-use agent that pairs an accessibility-tree plus vision grounding approach with a testing-oriented MCP surface, giving the thin browser and computer-use role a rare Android entry.
